header.name: Topics in Functional Analysis: Operator Algebras
header.description:
The course aims to provide a rigorous introduction to the theory of Banach algebras and C*-algebras, with an emphasis on structure, examples, and the foundational theorems that reveal the deep interplay between algebra, analysis, and operator theory. The course is divided into two chapters.

Chapter 1 develops the general theory of Banach algebras. We begin with the definition and a range of motivating examples drawn from function algebras and algebras of operators. We then introduce the spectrum of an element and the spectral radius, establishing fundamental results such as the Gelfand-Mazur theorem. The chapter culminates in the study of commutative Banach algebras, where we develop the Gelfand transform and prove the Gelfand representation theorem thereby connecting abstract commutative Banach algebras and algebras of continuous functions.

Chapter 2 focuses on C*-algebras, a highly structured class of Banach algebras arising naturally in operator theory. After introducing their definition and principal examples, we establish the characterisation of commutative C*-algebras via the Gelfand-Naimark theorem, which identifies them concretely with algebras of continuous functions on compact Hausdorff spaces. We then study positive elements in C*-algebras and develop the order structure they induce. The course concludes with a recapitulation of operator theory from the perspective of operator algebras, highlighting how classical results about operators on Hilbert spaces fit naturally into the C*-algebraic framework.
prerequisites_mandatory: MTH 552A (TFA: Operator theory on Hilbert spaces)

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to explain and analyze definitions and examples of Banach algebras, and compute and interpret the spectrum and spectral radius of elements in concrete settings.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to analyze the structure of commutative Banach algebras via the Gelfand transform and justify key structural results such as the Gelfand–Mazur theorem and the spectral permanence theorem.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to demonstrate foundational understanding of the defining properties of C*-algebras, including positive elements and the C*-identity, and interpret the characterisation of commutative C*-algebras through the Gelfand-Naimark theorem.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to apply the C*-algebraic framework to classical operator theory, construct proofs of central results within this framework, and evaluate how operator-theoretic concepts are unified and generalized through C*-algebra methods.

lecture_topics: The spectrum and spectral radius: Gelfand-Mazur theorem, Spectral permanence theorem
Commutative Banach algebras: The Gelfand transform, Gelfand theorem for commutative Banach algebras
The characterisation of commutative C*-algebras (the Gelfand-Naimark theorem)
Recapitulation of Operator Theory from the perspective of Operator Algebras
